The one-indexed Josephus function and its bridge to the accepted zero-indexed survivor module. The corpus module LeanFrontier/Combinatorics/Josephus.lean (submission josephus-survivor-binary-shift) numbers the circle from 0 and defines survivor by the shift-and-wrap recurrence survivor (n+1) = (survivor n + 2) % (n+1). This module treats the classical one-indexed convention: josephus is defined independently by the well-founded halving recursion J(2n) = 2 J(n) - 1, J(2n+1) = 2 J(n) + 1, and the two developments are reconciled by the bridge josephus n = survivor n + 1 for n nonzero. Because the two functions arise from different recursions - one steps the circle size by one, the other halves it - the bridge is a genuine theorem, and it cross-validates both formalizations. The remaining public statements are those with no counterpart in the accepted module: positivity, oddness of the survivor's number (the first pass eliminates every even number), josephus (2^m) = 1, the bound josephus n <= n, and the fixed-point characterization josephus n = n iff n = 2^m - 1, i.e. person n survives exactly when the binary expansion of n is all ones. The mathematics is classical (the closed form is Concrete Mathematics section 1.3) and is not claimed as new.

Relation to the corpus and absence evidence. This submission supersedes the original content of this pull request, which predates the merge of the zero-indexed module and added a module at the same path; replacing that file would remove six accepted entrypoints and is rejected by the receiver as a corpus regression, as the maintainer verified in a probe pull request. Of the two routes the maintainer offered, this takes import-and-extend: the accepted module is imported unchanged, the halving recurrences and both closed forms for josephus are proved from the definition but kept private (as public statements they would only mirror survivor_two_mul, survivor_two_mul_add_one and survivor_two_pow_add through the bridge), and the public surface consists of the bridge plus the five statements the maintainer confirmed have no counterpart: no parity statement, no positivity, no upper bound, no power-of-two evaluation and no fixed-point characterization exists in the corpus in any form, in either convention. Over the pinned Mathlib tree at v4.33.0-rc1, josephus and A006257 have zero case-insensitive hits, as recorded for the accepted zero-indexed submission.

Implementation. The definition recurses on n / 2 with termination by Nat.div_lt_self. The bridge is a two-line rewrite connecting the private Nat.log closed form of josephus with the accepted survivor_eq_two_mul_sub_two_pow_log; josephus_le is derived through the bridge from the accepted survivor_lt_self, so the two theories genuinely feed each other. Oddness and the fixed-point characterization come from the private log form; positivity is a strong induction on the private halving recurrences. Imports are the accepted Josephus module, Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Parity and Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log.

Verification beyond the receiver. In a scratch file outside the repository the bridge was checked by evaluation for every n from 1 to 200, and the classical n = 41 story evaluates to (josephus, survivor) = (19, 18). The n = 41 instance is kept in the module as an example, not a public theorem.

Not included. The halving recurrences and closed forms as public statements (mirrors of accepted entrypoints); the elimination order as a permutation and the general step-k recurrence, which need a circle model of their own.

Provenance. Produced by the same agent session as the six merged submissions of this series, from the repository's TRY-LEANFRONTIER launcher. The original module predates the zero-indexed merge; the maintainer pointed out the collision on the pull request, the agent chose the import-and-extend route from the two offered, and the rework was machine-produced. Proofs use well-founded recursion, strong induction, omega, and the named corpus and Mathlib lemmas.
